### Marital Grace
Author: Charles R. Swindoll
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/todays-insight-chuck-swindoll/todays-insight-september-2-2023.html
Passage: Ephesians 5:33
Points:
- Operating in divine grace prevents spouses from controlling or constantly appeasing one another.
- Grace builds up dignity and encourages rather than fostering jealousy and suspicion.
- Insecurity and possessiveness can smother a spouse and damage marital trust.
- Confessing destructive habits invites God's grace to cleanse and renew the relationship.

### The Sacrificial Quotient of Giving
Author: Adrian Rogers
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/loveworthfinding/love-worth-finding-august-20.html
Passage: Ephesians 5:25
Points:
- Husbands are commanded to pattern their love after Christ's sacrifice for His church.
- True marital love demands a readiness to lay down one's life.
- A husband's calling includes providing for and protecting his wife.
- Spouses are challenged to assess their willingness to give selflessly to one another.

### The Vocation of Wives
Author: Ligonier Ministries
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/vocation-of-wives
Passage: Ephesians 5:22-24
Points:
- Scripture assigns husbands a leadership role while calling wives to submit to their husbands.
- A wife's submission is specific to her own husband, not to men in general.
- Biblical submission is not absolute and ends if a husband commands sin or forbids righteousness.
- Submission does not silence a wife's input or wise counsel in household matters.
- Believing wives are called to show patience toward imperfect husbands seeking to follow Christ.

### Day 305: Ephesians 5:25–33
Author: Beth Moore
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/plus/books/portraits-of-devotion/portraits-of-devotion-day-305-ephesians-5-2533.html
Passage: Ephesians 5:25-33
Points:
- Christ serves as the supreme role model for husbands called to love selflessly.
- Husbands are charged with loving in ways that foster purity and holiness in marriage.
- Loving a spouse as one's own body produces mutual peace and flourishing.
- A healthy biblical marriage relies upon a submissive wife, a loving husband, and Christ as head.
